ask.1: can we measure, per paper, whether Qwen3-32B holds its authors, and trust the numbers?
ask.12: is the author signal about this paper, or just easy names?
ask.34: which readout can see the author signal, and how early?
ask.44: when does the paper information arrive, and when is it used?
ask.52: which part of the name, and which cue in the prompt, carries it?
ask.62: what do the four lines add up to?
ask.65: if the middle layers do not hold the name, what do they hold?
ask.71: where does the information travel, and who writes the name?
ask.77: is it the title’s meaning, or the identity of this paper?
ask.82: are author names hidden in the middle layers, and are made-up names near-misses?
ask.90: does recognising a paper change how strong the signal is, or when it arrives?

so.11: one prompt, one score (rank of the true name among all tokens) and true vs 5 false titles give a per-paper measure, compared within citation bins with team-cluster CIs. [method]
so.33: the signal is paper-specific: the true title beats false titles for every group, recognised papers lead only at the output (+0.21), and writing needs about 276× the exposure that recognising does. [confirmed]
so.43: lenses read names only late; a probe at the title reads a little paper-specific signal early, and at the name positions a probe beats the J-lens on the same scale at L40 and L48. [fairly solid]
so.51: it arrives early (mainly L40–L50, half by L45) and is said late (steepest rise L57–L61, written by the MLPs). [settled]
so.61: the surname and full given names carry it, initials little; a given first initial helps; a true co-author helps through the co-author network, not this paper. [confirmed]
so.64: read early, said late: the shelf is mostly filled by L50, and the name comes out only at the end. [summary]
so.70: the middle layers hold the question and the paper’s facts, but nothing beyond what the title text gives at L4 [descriptive]; before L48 only faint, scattered author traces [exploratory]
so.76: title → name positions through the name ← title attention edge (L44–L55, small) [fairly solid] → the L52–L56 MLPs carry the paper [descriptive] → the L57–L61 MLPs write the name [settled]
so.81: a same-meaning made-up title recovers 75% of the gap; the real title adds +0.11, so H2 is partly supported and meaning explains most of the signal. [confirmed]
so.89: on the same scale a probe reads more of the author than the J-lens at L40 and L48 (H3 supported) [fairly solid]; made-up names are not confused neighbours [exploratory]
so.94: recognition changes the size, hardly the timing; the higher recovery in B is a small-denominator effect. [confirmed]
so.97: one model, subsamples for interventions and a few post-hoc locks; none of the checks reverses a conclusion. [limits]
